newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may try new space docking or let craft burn.
newsitem.headline: Russia may try new space docking or let craft burn.

text.p: Russia was considering on Wednesday whether to renew efforts to dock an unmanned cargo ship with the space station Mir or let the Progress-M-33 craft burn up in the atmosphere, a space industry official said.
The vessel failed to complete a planned docking with Mir on Tuesday in the latest setback to Russia's space programme.
"We may try another docking attempt in two or three days, under more favourable ballistic conditions," Sergei Gromov, an aide to the chief designer of Energiya rocket corporation, told Reuters.
"But we will not lose much if the docking fails and we will send the Progress to burn up in the atmosphere...the ship is unloaded and ready to be destroyed."
He said there has always been some doubt that the docking would be successful. The flight of the Progress-M-33 was fully controlled from earth and it posed no danger, he said.

Tuesday's failed docking was the second hitch in just over a week to trouble the 11-year-old Mir, which has already outlived its expected lifespan. On February 23, a fire broke out on board, forcing the crew to don gas masks.
The Progress, in orbit since November 1996, had undocked from Mir on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 craft which brought a replacement crew.
It was decided afterwards to redock the Progress because it still had some fuel on board and could help adjust the trajectory of the ageing Mir.
But Gromov said the amount of fuel left on the cargo ship was small and not crucially important for the Mir, while Mir's orbit did not need to be adjusted immediately.

"The main reason to dock them is to make a sort of garbage ship out of the Progress. It will be loaded with rubbish as it will burn up sooner or later anyway. The other reason is to see how long it can work," Gromov said.
The Progress will sooner or later be sent into the atmosphere, where it is expected to burn over the Southern part of the Pacific Ocean, Gromov said.
Russia plans to launch a new cargo craft later this month with supplies for the cosmonauts and fuel, Gromov said. This launch has been delayed several times, and Gromov said no new date had been set.

Russia's space agency is suffering a severe cash crisis which last week prompted it to postpone the launch of its first contribution to a planned international space station, Alpha, which will replace Mir.
